gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each hybrid mic actually keeps when you move it to an audio interface over XLR. The Rode PodMic USB's XLR port goes dead while USB-C is plugged in. In XLR mode it also loses APHEX processing and its headphone jack, and a Behringer UMC204HD had to be turned all the way up to drive it. The Shure MV7+ runs USB and XLR at the same time, and its XLR feed is unprocessed.
standout_why: I could not read the body text of either cited MusicRadar page (best-podcasting-microphones and best-usb-microphones): both came back with only the title. I also did not read the uncited top results (soundlevel.app, thepostflow, thetoolshelf, lensandmic, itechguides, soundbounty), so this score is less certain. What I could check is the answer ChatGPT built from those results. Its table marks 'Headphone monitoring: Yes' for the MV7+, PodMic USB and Q9U, and 'Auto gain: Yes' for the MV7+, with no USB-only caveat. It recommends the PodMic USB as 'best value' while telling the shopper to plan on 'the ability to upgrade to an audio interface later'. Nothing it showed says the PodMic's XLR and USB can't run together, that APHEX and the headphone jack stop working over XLR, or that the MV7+'s XLR output carries no processing.
decides: If the shopper plans to move to an interface later, which is the reason ChatGPT gave for buying a hybrid, the PodMic USB's 'value' pick gets weaker. Over XLR it is a plain dynamic mic with about 1.4 mV/Pa output and none of the features ChatGPT credited it with. ComputerBase had to max out a UMC204HD to drive it, with audible noise. The MV7+ gives a 2 dB hotter XLR signal (1.78 mV/Pa) and can feed a processed USB stream and a raw XLR stream at the same time, for example a recorder plus a stream. That backs the MV7+ for anyone who will really use the XLR side. For USB-only buyers the PodMic USB pick still holds.

findings.label: XLR output sensitivity
findings.note: Shure's US product page (shure.com/en-US/products/microphones/mv7) does not list sensitivity, and the Shure user guide page returned no text. I used the Thomann spec list, which also gives USB-C as -33 dBFS/Pa at minimum gain. This is the white colourway; I assume the same transducer as the black.

findings.label: USB and XLR used at the same time / processing on XLR
findings.value: Both outputs active at once; XLR carries the unprocessed analogue signal, unaffected by software settings
findings.note: Thomann's wording: 'Both outputs are active simultaneously' and the XLR signal is 'passive and unaffected by software settings'. Shure's own product page and its 2024-04-09 newsroom release do not say either way. Auto Level, Denoiser and Popper Stopper are set in MOTIV Mix over USB.

findings.note: Fills the 'Not listed on Shure's product page' cell on our current page, with a retailer spec as the source. USB A/D is 16 or 24 bit at 44.1 or 48 kHz.

findings.label: XLR sensitivity
findings.source_title: Rode PodMic USB Review / Test – Podcastage
findings.note: Podcastage lists 'Sensitivity: -57dB'. -57 dBV/Pa works out to about 1.4 mV/Pa, 2 dB below the MV7+ (1.78 mV/Pa). The Rode US product page has an empty Specifications section, and I could not read the text of Rode's datasheet PDF.

findings.label: What works in XLR mode
findings.value: APHEX DSP and the Revolution preamp are USB-only. Over XLR the 3.5 mm jack cannot monitor (the interface has to). A Behringer UMC204HD's input knob had to be fully up, with higher noise.
findings.source_title: Rode PodMic USB im Test – ComputerBase
findings.note: Michael Schäfer, ComputerBase, 2023-07-25: 'Wird das Mikrofon hingegen über die XLR-Verbindung genutzt, muss das jeweilige Audio-Interface als Monitorausgabe dienen' ('when the mic is used over XLR, the audio interface has to serve as the monitor output'), and 'Analog wird der Eingangsregler des Audio-Interfaces nicht selten am Anschlag stehen – mit entsprechend hohem Rauschen' ('in analog use the interface's input knob is often at its stop, with correspondingly high noise'). He heard no sound difference between USB and XLR. Rode's US page ties the Revolution Preamp and APHEX to 'the digital USB output'.

findings.label: XLR sensitivity
findings.note: Maker page: 'Max Sensitivity: XLR -57 dBV/Pa (1 kHz)'. Also 50 Hz to 20 kHz, 250 Ω, USB 24-bit up to 96 kHz, and 'Mute button controls both USB and XLR outputs.' The page shows 'Coming Soon / unavailable' with no price.

findings.label: Normalised XLR output
findings.value: MV7+ 1.78 mV/Pa; PodMic USB about 1.4 mV/Pa; Q9U about 1.4 mV/Pa
findings.note: Converted with mV = 1000 × 10^(dBV/20): -55 dBV gives 1.78 mV and -57 dBV gives 1.41 mV. All three are low-output dynamics on XLR. The MV7+ is 2 dB hotter. That gap is real but small next to the feature differences above.
